title: Intro to REBEL
text: REBEL R package analyzing cell-type specific differential expression longitudinal repeated measure scRNA-seq studies. package implements method using linear mixed model (LMM) framework empirical Bayes process improve estimation residual random effect variance sharing information across genes. method uses either cell-level data, case random intercepts subject sample used account correlation data, pseudo-bulk data, case cell-level counts aggregated across cells random intercept subject included model. Models can fit multiple fixed effects including group variables vary subject level (.e. disease vs control), variables vary within subject, time related variables (.e. baseline, follow-), interaction effects. Hypothesis testing performed model coefficients linear contrasts using Kenward-Roger degrees freedom estimated using empirical Bayes variance estimates.

title: Intro to REBEL
text: REBEL designed test differential expression covariates within single cell type subpopulation cells. package workflow begins using scRNA-seq data processed data filtered cell type interest. Figure 1 shows basic workflow REBEL package can split three sections: Data preprocessing: aggregating data (pseudo-bulk option ) applying normalizing transformation counts. Fitting REBEL models: fitting LMM’s, calculating empirical Bayes variance estimates, calculating parameters used Kenward Roger’s degrees freedom method. Hypothesis testing: performing tests differential expression model fixed effects. provide depth process using real example.

text: use data simulated using rescueSim package, can used simulate single-cell type longitudinal scRNA-seq data. use preset simulation parameters available package, parameters can also estimated empirical data. simulated data two group (ex. control group, treatment group), two timepoint (ex. baseline, follow-) design simulate 5 subjects group (10 total subjects, 20 samples). Samples simulated 50 150 cells number cells per sample drawn discrete uniform distribution. decrease computation times example, analyze first 100 genes simulated data.
code: library(rescueSim) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(REBEL)  ## Set seed for reproducibility set.seed=24  ## Load present  data("RecAM_params")  ## Adjust parameters RecAM_params <- updateRescueSimParams(     paramObj = RecAM_params,     paramValues = list(         twoGroupDesign = T,         maxCellsPerSamp=150,         minCellsPerSamp=50,         propDE=.2,         deLog2FC=1     ) )  ## Simulate data dat <- simRescueData(RecAM_params)  ## Function returns a single cell experiment object class(dat) ## [1] "SingleCellExperiment" ## attr(,"package") ## [1] "SingleCellExperiment" ## Remove genes that have more than 75% 0's idx_rm=which(rowSums(assay(dat, "counts")==0)>(.75*ncol(dat))) dat=dat[-idx_rm,]  ## Subset to first 100 genes dat=dat[1:100,]  ## The raw counts are located in the counts assay of the object assay(dat, "counts")[1:5,1:5] ##         cell_1 cell_2 cell_3 cell_4 cell_5 ## NOC2L        2      1      1      2      1 ## ISG15        2      1     16      6     15 ## SDF4         0      0      4      3      0 ## B3GALT6      0      0      0      0      3 ## UBE2J2       1      0      1      1      3 ## Data also contains cell-level meta data head(colData(dat)) ## DataFrame with 6 rows and 4 columns ##           sampleID   subjectID        time       group ##        <character> <character> <character> <character> ## cell_1     sample1    subject1       time0      group0 ## cell_2     sample1    subject1       time0      group0 ## cell_3     sample1    subject1       time0      group0 ## cell_4     sample1    subject1       time0      group0 ## cell_5     sample1    subject1       time0      group0 ## cell_6     sample1    subject1       time0      group0

title: Intro to REBEL
text: model fitting process includes three steps. First LMM models fit using rebelLMM function. cell-level data, models fit using random intercept terms sample subject well specified fixed effect terms. utilize lmerTest package fit individual models. Next, using rebelEmpBayes function, residual random effect variances re-estimated using empirical Bayes process information across genes borrowed get accurate estimates. Finally, parameter estimates used Kenward-Roger degrees freedom method calculated using rebelKRParams function. draw pbkrtest package estimate values, make adjustments empirical Bayes estimates used get parameter estimates. also simplify estimation process making specific random intercept models, decreases computation time considerably. provide wrapper function rebelFit combines three functions one convenient function. , outline function arguments used rebelFit. Now use fit REBEL models using rebelFit. fit model time group fixed effects well interaction effect. resulting object class RebelFit holds information function call, model parameters model fits. table describes slots RebelFit object.

code: ## Read in cell-level data (scTransform normalized data saved in normcounts slot) data("RecAM_sim_sce")  ## Just use first 10 genes RecAM_sim_sce_fil <- RecAM_sim_sce[1:10,]  ## Fit models with time, group and time/group interaction effect cell_fit <- rebelFit(object=RecAM_sim_sce_fil,                      fixedEffects = ~time*group,                      subjectVariable ="subjectID", sampleVariable = "sampleID",                      pseudoBulk = FALSE) #> [1] "Fitting LMM Models" #> [1] "Getting Empirical Bayes Estimates" #> [1] "Getting Parameters for Kenward-Rogers method"  ## Run test on interaction coefficient interaction_coef_test=rebelTest(cell_fit, coef="timetime1:groupgroup1")  ## Run test on interaction coefficient using a contrast interaction_contrast_test=rebelTest(cell_fit, contrast = c(0,0,0,1))  ## Using coefficient and contrast to test interaction produce identical results identical(interaction_coef_test, interaction_contrast_test) #> [1] TRUE  ##  multi-dimensional contrast (F-test) contrast_mat <- rbind(c(0, 1, 0, 0),                    c(0, 0, 1, 0),                    c(0, 0, 0, 1)) ## simultaneous test of all coefficients joint_contrast_test=rebelTest(cell_fit, contrast = contrast_mat)
